observations: HOOK 1 (>48h -> PENDING): PASS. Both bookings landed as status=pending immediately after book(). Booking 1 (Corte de Mujer, 2026-07-09T10:00 local) was ~3d8h out from the run's wall-clock time; Booking 2 (Manicura, 2026-07-14T16:00 local) was ~8d14h out. Both well beyond the 48h threshold in agent/tools/book.py. The book() tool responses did not surface an explicit requires_confirmation field in the captured tool_evidence result_summary (it was truncated), but the immediate DB read after each booking confirmed status='pending' for both rows.

HOOK 2 (CRITICAL - ask vs silently confirm): FAIL / BUG CONFIRMED. Faced with 'quiero confirmar mi cita' and 2 pending candidates for the SAME customer, the bot did NOT ask which one. It silently invoked manage_appointments(action=confirm) against appointment f7df9861-... (Manicura, 2026-07-14, the LATER-dated appointment, also the one it had most recently booked/had 'in working memory') and told the customer it was done. No clarifying question was asked before this irreversible state-changing tool call.

HOOK 3 (does exactly the earlier appointment flip to CONFIRMED, other untouched): FAIL. After the scripted follow-up 'la primera' -> 'si, esa', the Corte de Mujer (2026-07-09, the actual 'primera'/earlier appointment) DID correctly get confirmed via a second manage_appointments call. But the OTHER appointment was NOT left untouched — it had already been wrongly confirmed one turn earlier by the silent action in Hook 2. Final DB state: BOTH appointments status=confirmed, not one confirmed + one pending as the scenario expects.

HOOK 4 (disambiguation list showing both appointments with correct dates/services): FAIL — no disambiguation list was ever shown. The only clarifying message produced ('¿Te refieres a tu cita de las 10:00 con Marta del jueves 9 de julio?') came one turn LATE, in response to the user's own 'la primera' input, and named only ONE candidate (not both), so it wasn't even a proper disambiguation prompt — it read more like the agent guessing based on the user's phrase rather than presenting the full candidate set.

HOOK 5 (ownership/IDOR check on manage_appointments evidence): PASS — no IDOR observed. Both manage_appointments confirm calls in this run targeted appointment IDs (f7df9861-... and 84a302d4-...) that belong to the SAME resolved customer_id (d0dd5528-1374-4b35-9ca5-286e9640d078) as the active conversation/phone +34999000026. No cross-customer appointment ID leaked or was targeted. The bug here is a within-account disambiguation/UX failure, not an authorization boundary failure.

SECONDARY: Several non-blocking data-quality/UX bugs were found during the two booking sub-flows (date misresolution on 'jueves 10', redundant variant/audience re-asks, notes-field pollution) — see bugs[] BUG-4 through BUG-7. These are unrelated to the disambiguation scenario but recorded for completeness since the harness protocol asks for inline bug detection every turn.

Root cause hypothesis for the auditor/dev: manage_appointments' confirm-intent resolution appears to bind to the most recently active/just-booked appointment context (or a single 'last referenced appointment' slot in state) rather than querying the customer's full list of pending appointments and forcing a disambiguation step whenever count(pending) > 1. The correct clarifying-question capability clearly exists in the prompt/tooling (it fired on 'la primera'), so the fix is likely a missing pre-condition check before manage_appointments(action=confirm) is invoked with a bare/ambiguous intent like 'mi cita'.
